attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his own view.

semantics.note: The sentence sits inside a passage introduced as 'Here's my own guess', and the same passage goes on with 'may'. A guess is graded, low-confidence language, like 'I suspect'. The normalisation drops this qualifier and records the modality as a firm 'will'. Target OpenAI and the copyright scope are otherwise fine.

contract.note: The contract scores this as a firm forecast on a plain reading. Plain readings apply only to firm language. Because Marcus framed it as a guess, it should not be scored. Even read as firm, 'heavily' and 'potential future profits' have no measure, baseline, or deadline.

evidence.note: News Corp's own announcement of a licensing deal with OpenAI (May 2024). It gives no payment amount and no effect on profits.
Oct 2025 SDNY order denying OpenAI's motion to dismiss in the copyright MDL. It shows the litigation is ongoing but awards no damages and says nothing about profits.

reviews.rationale: Marcus presented this as 'my own guess', which is hedged, low-confidence language, so the policy does not score it. Even read as a firm forecast, it has no deadline. The packet shows a licensing deal and ongoing litigation, but no payout totals or profit comparison, so it would be unresolved at most.
